lesson_title: Twelve Seconds That Changed the World
hook_text: The first aeroplane flight lasted only twelve seconds, shorter than the time it takes to tie your shoes.
clip_script: A cold, windy beach in the United States, 17 December 1903. A strange machine made of wood, wire and cloth sits on a wooden rail. Orville Wright lies flat on the lower wing. The engine coughs, the propellers spin, and the machine rolls forward, lifts, and flies. Twelve seconds. Thirty-seven metres. His brother Wilbur runs beside it. Two bicycle makers had done what people had dreamed of for thousands of years.
visual_style: Whiteboard drawing of the Wright Flyer on its rail, a stopwatch counting twelve seconds, a dotted flight path, then a modern jet drawn above it.
mood: Thrilling and hopeful, like the moment before a big jump.
pacing: Tense build-up on the beach, a burst of joy at take-off, then a quick jump to today.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and fold a paper plane to test how wings work.
